comment: What each host does with every prop, one row per attribute.
The list of attributes is not maintained here: scripts/scrape_props.py reads
it out of React Native and writes docs/react-native-props.json, and
scripts/check_support.js renders the page from the two together. A prop added
upstream therefore has no status, and the check fails until somebody says what
this platform does with it -- which is the whole reason the list is scraped.
Statuses: yes, partial, no, upstream (ReactCommon consumes it), ignored
`reads` on a row names the spelling that counts as evidence for a prop a host
reaches through something else -- resolveBorderMetrics, allShadows,
resolveTransform -- so the check stays tight for everything else.
(deliberately not implemented). Anything but `yes` everywhere needs a `why`,
which is a key into `whys` below.
A grep cannot prove behaviour and this file does not pretend to: what proves a
prop behaves is the scenario in scripts/integration_test.py that exercises it
on every host. The check does assert that a host claiming a prop reads it.
A prop that exists only on React Native main has no row here on purpose: the
inventory is scraped from the pinned release, so the row appears -- and this
file is asked for a status -- on the commit that moves the pin.

win-stock-cursors.text: six keywords have no stock cursor

mac-dropshadow.text: macOS draws the first of a list

cannot-arrive.text: only the iOS view config declares it, and the two desktops would draw different corners

no-group.text: no public way to composite a subtree as a group

hints.text: performance hints, and one cannot arrive

reactcommon.text: ReactCommon consumes it, and a scenario proves it here

text-ignored.text: on the ignored list, with the call named

text-shadow-one.text: one shadow per paragraph, not per fragment

text-ios.text: iOS's own, with no desktop equivalent

measurelines.text: the cxx TextLayoutManager has no measureLines

a11y-ios.text: iOS's own, with no desktop equivalent

win-textscale.text: the scale is there, as UISettings.TextScaleFactor, and needs WinRT

text-decoration-style.text: each engine draws the styles it has: Pango no dots or dashes, Core Text no wavy; the Win32 renderer draws all five

win-textvariant.text: DWRITE_FONT_FEATURE_TAG takes the same tags core resolves

gtk-accessible-id.text: GTK publishes an accessible id from 4.22; CI's 4.14 carries it and cannot publish it

a11y-language.text: GTK has no accessible language property; macOS 26 for a view-wide one, UIA wants an LCID

win-reading-direction.text: IDWriteTextLayout::SetReadingDirection, and a natural alignment that follows it

win-reading-order.text: UIA has no reading-order property: the tree order is the order

yoga.text: Yoga computes it and every host applies the frame it answers with

android-only.text: Android's own: ReactCommon declares it in that platform's host props

vertical-align.text: the paragraph moves in its box; an inline view inside one does not

android-view.text: Android's shadow prop, declared in that platform's host props

image-android.text: Android's own, and recorded as ignored with the rest of that group

image-ios.text: iOS's resizable slicing, with no desktop equivalent

image-placeholder.text: no host draws a placeholder while an image loads

image-events.text: every host emits load events unconditionally, as iOS does

image-analytics.text: Meta's own analytics tag, which nothing outside their infrastructure reads

ti-ios.text: iOS's own, with no desktop equivalent

ti-soft-keyboard.text: a soft keyboard, which a desktop does not have

ti-return-key.text: the label on a soft keyboard's return key, and no desktop has one

ti-context-menu.text: GTK covers the pointer and not the Menu key; AppKit covers a multiline field and not the shared field editor of a single-line one

ti-ignored.text: on the ignored list in that file, with what each would take

ti-trait.text: read through the iOS variant's trait of the same name, which has its own row

ti-default-value.text: TextInput.js folds it into `text` before a host sees anything

ti-colours.text: a Win32 EDIT draws its selection in COLOR_HIGHLIGHT, which no message changes: it wants a windowless RichEdit

win-upper-only.text: ES_UPPERCASE covers `characters`; an EDIT cannot find a word or a sentence

win-no-spellcheck.text: carried and reported; a Win32 EDIT has no spell checker and ISpellChecker draws nothing

sv-zoom.text: no host zooms, and a desktop has no obvious gesture for it

sv-bounce.text: a desktop scroll view has no rubber band, so there is nothing to turn off

sv-ios.text: iOS's own, with no desktop equivalent

sv-keyboard.text: a soft keyboard, which a desktop does not have

sv-axis.text: the axis is derived from the content's size, so the hint goes unread

sv-deceleration.text: GTK's momentum reads it; AppKit takes the system's own deceleration and Windows has no momentum yet

sv-indicator-default.text: white is white; iOS's 'default' differs from 'black' only by a white border around the thumb, which these hosts do not draw

text-selection.text: the paragraph is selected and copied; an inline view inside one is not

areas.note: What an <Image> does that is not one prop. Its props are scraped, in the ImageProps section above.
